Interim Financial Report \n\n The interim financial report is unaudited and has been prepared in compliance with Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (\"MFRS\") 134, Interim Financial Reporting issued by the Malaysian Accounting Standards Board, Paragraph 9.22 and Appendix 9B of the Listing Requirements of Bursa Malaysia Securities Berhad. \n\n The interim financial report should be read in conjunction with the audited financial statements of the Group for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 and the accompanying explanatory notes attached to this interim financial report. \n\n The significant accounting policies and method of computation adopted in the interim financial report are consistent with those adopted in the annual financial statements for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 except for the adoption of the following MFRSs:- \n\n Effective for annual periods beginning on or after \n\n Amendments to MFRS 9 and MFRS 7 Amendments to the Classification and Measurement of Financial Instruments\n\n Amendments to MFRS 9 and MFRS 7 Contracts Referencing Nature-dependent Electricity\n\n 1 January 2026 \n\n 1 January 2026 \n\n Annual Improvements to MFRS Accounting Standards - Volume 11 1 January 2026 \n\n The initial application of the above MFRSs did not have any significant impacts on the financial statements. \n\n The Group has not applied the following MFRSs which have been issued as at the end of reporting period but are not yet effective:- \n\n MFRS (issued as at the end of the reporting period) \n\n Effective for annual periods beginning on or after \n\n MFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements 1 January 2027 MFRS 19 Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures 1 January 2027 \n\n Amendments to operations \n\n The Group's operation is dependent on the cyclical trend of the semiconductors and electronics industries. \n\n A3 Unusual items affecting assets, liabilities, equity, net income or cash flows \n\n There were no unusual items affecting assets, liabilities, equity, net income or cash flows during the current interim period. \n\n A4 Material changes in estimates \n\n There were no changes in estimates of amounts reported in prior interim period of the current financial year or changes in estimate of amounts reported in prior financial year. \n\n A5 Debts and equity securities \n\n During the current quarter, the Company issued 1,123,800, 172,400 and 285,800 new ordinary shares at issued prices of RM3.4628, RM3.7937 and RM3.4921 respectively pursuant to the Employee Shares Grant Scheme (\"SGS\"). \n\n Save as disclosed above, there were no other issuances, cancellations, repurchases, resale or repayments of debts and equity securities during the current quarter under review. \n\n A6 Dividend paid \n\n During the financial period, the Company paid an interim tax exempt dividend of 0.63 sen per share amounting to RM11,927,401 for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, paid on 16 January 2026. \n\n A7 Segment reporting \n\n No segment reporting has been prepared as the Group is principally engaged in development and production of vision inspection systems and printed circuit board assemblies for microprocessor applications. \n\n A8 Material events subsequent to the end of the quarter \n\n There were no material events subsequent to the end of the current reporting period that have not been reflected in the interim financial report. \n\n A9 Changes in the composition of the Group \n\n The Company had on 1 April 2026 incorporated a wholly-owned subsidiary namely, ViTrox Technical Academy Sdn. Bhd. (\"VTA\") by way of subscribing 10 ordinary shares in VTA for a total cash consideration of RM10. Its intended principal activity is providing Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) dedicated to establishing industrial mastery centers that deliver specialised training, competency-based assessments, and industry-recognised certifications in high-tech manufacturing and digital skills. \n\n Save as disclosed above, there were no material changes in the composition of the Group during the current quarter under review. \n\n A10 Contingencies \n\n There were no contingent assets or liabilities for the Group since 31 December 2025 up to 30 June 2026. \n\n A11 Contractual commitments \n\n 30-Jun-26 30-Jun-25 \n\n RM'000 RM'000 \n\n Acquisition of property, plant and equipment 50,416 46,610 \n\n A12 Significant related party transactions \n\n There were no significant related party transactions during the current quarter under review. \n\n A13 Financial instruments \n\n1. Derivatives \n\n As at 30 June 2026, the Group's outstanding derivatives are as follows:- \n\n Forward exchange contracts - at fair value \n\n RM'000 \n\n - Current liabilities 4,013 \n\n Derivatives consist of forward exchange contracts which are used to hedge the exposure to currency risk. The Group does not apply hedge accounting. As at 30 June 2026, the Group had contracts with financial institutions due within 1 year to buy RM188,750,000 and sell USD47,400,000 at contractual forward rates. \n\n The fair values of forward exchange contracts were quoted by the financial institutions, which normally measured the fair values using present value technique by discounting the differences between contractual forward prices and observable current market forward prices using risk-free interest rate (i.e. Level 2). \n2. Gains/(Losses) arising from fair value changes of financial liabilities \n\n T here were no gains/(losses) arising from fair value changes of financial liabilities for the current quarter and period ended 30 June 2026.\n3. Fair value \n\n The Group uses valuation techniques that are appropriate in the circumstances and for which sufficient data are available to measure fair value, maximising the use of relevant observable inputs and minimising the use of unobservable inputs. \n\n The inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value are categorised into the following levels of fair value hierarchy:- \n\n1. Level 1 - quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the entity can access at the measurement date. \n2. Level 2 - inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. \n3. Level 3 - unobservable inputs for the asset or liability. \n\n As at end of the current quarter under review, the carrying amounts of receivables, cash and cash equivalents and payables which are short-term in nature or repayable on demand are reasonable approximations of fair values. \n\n The fair value of long term loans are measured using present value technique by discounting the expected future cash flows using observable current market interest rates for similar liabilities (i.e. Level 2). The fair values measured are considered to be reasonably close to the carrying amount reported as the observable current market interest rates also approximate to the effective interest rates of term loans. \n\n The fair value of forward exchange contracts were quoted by the financial institutions, which normally measured the fair values using present value technique by discounting the differences between contractual forward prices and observable current market forward prices using risk-free interest rate (i.e. Level 2). \n\n There were no transfers between levels of fair value hierarchy during the current quarter under review. \n\n B1 Review of performance \n\n Current quarter \n\n Corresponding preceding quarter \n\n ended \n\n 30-Jun-26 \n\n 30-Jun-25 \n\n Changes \n\n Revenue \n\n 374,915 \n\n 183,043 \n\n 191,872 \n\n 104.8% \n\n Profit before tax \n\n 99,946 \n\n 37,907 \n\n 62,039 \n\n 163.7% \n\n Profit for the financial period \n\n 84,495 \n\n 27,807 \n\n 56,688 \n\n 203.9% \n\n Profit attributable to owners of \n\n the Company \n\n 85,043 \n\n 28,133 \n\n 56,910 \n\n 202.3% \n\n The Group's revenue for the quarter under review achieved a stellar expansion of 104.8% or RM191.9 million, surging from RM183.0 million in the corresponding preceding quarter to RM374.9 million. This remarkable top-line performance was primarily driven by explosive Artificial Intelligence (\"AI\") infrastructure demand, our strategic focus into high-value, resilient markets like automotive, and consumer electronics and accelerated global supply chain restructuring which has deepened customer engagements. Our focus on advanced packaging and high-precision inspection solutions directly addresses the increasing complexities of AI accelerators and High Bandwidth Memory (\"HBM\") mirroring the strong momentum seen in the broader semiconductors and electronics manufacturing sector and enabling us to expand our output far beyond the previous year's low baseline. \n\n Profit before tax (\"PBT\") for the individual quarter surged by 163.7% or RM62.0 million, soaring to RM99.9 million from RM37.9 million due to structural manufacturing scale and a highly favourable product mix. Profit after tax (\"PAT\") rose by 203.9% or RM56.7 million, increasing from RM27.8 million to RM84.5 million. This bottom-line outperformance reflects exceptional operational optimization across the facilities alongside the sustained positive impact of income tax exemption enjoyed by the key subsidiary ViTrox Technologies Sdn. Bhd. (\"VTSB\"). \n\n Corresponding \n\n Current \n\n period-to-date ended \n\n preceding \n\n period-to-date ended \n\n 30-Jun-26 \n\n 30-Jun-25 \n\n 641,966 \n\n 324,161 \n\n 317,805 \n\n 98.0% \n\n Profit before tax \n\n 161,605 \n\n 65,320 \n\n 96,285 \n\n 147.4% \n\n Profit for the financial period \n\n 135,278 \n\n 51,713 \n\n 83,565 \n\n 161.6% \n\n Profit attributable to owners of \n\n the Company \n\n 136,241 \n\n 52,293 \n\n 83,948 \n\n 160.5% \n\n The Group cumulative revenue achieved a robust expansion of 98.0% to RM642.0 million, a result of our steadfast commitment to disciplined execution and long-term value creation. We have successfully seized the momentum from strong AI infrastructure demands, alongside growing needs in the automotive and consumer electronics sectors. By leveraging our deep and broad customer base spanning over 30 countries, we continue to deliver advanced Automated Board Inspection (\"ABI\") and Machine Vision System (\"MVS\") solutions that meet the evolving requirements of our global partners with humility and focus. \n\n In tandem with this growth, cumulative PBT rose by 147.4% to RM161.6 million, while PAT climbed 161.6% to RM135.3 million. These results underscore our commitment to operational excellence and disciplined cost management, securing our strong financial position as we scale. \n\n B2 Variation of results against immediate preceding quarter \n\n Current quarter ended \n\n Immediate preceding \n\n 30-Jun-26 \n\n 31-Mar-26 \n\n 374,915 \n\n 267,051 \n\n 107,864 \n\n 40.4% \n\n Profit before tax \n\n 99,946 \n\n 61,659 \n\n 38,287 \n\n 62.1% \n\n Profit for the financial period \n\n 84,495 \n\n 50,782 \n\n 33,713 \n\n 66.4% \n\n Profit attributable to owners of \n\n the Company \n\n 85,043 \n\n 51,197 \n\n 33,846 \n\n 66.1% \n\n On a sequential basis, the Group's revenue expanded by 40.4% or RM107.9 million, ascending from RM267.1 million in the immediate preceding quarter to RM374.9 million. This strong top-line improvement was fundamentally propelled by accelerating shipment deliveries and robust customer pull-ins within both our ABI and MVS segments. This decisive sequential growth emphasizes superior production execution and signals a powerful close to the traditional post-peak transition phase. \n\n PBT grew sequentially by 62.1% or RM38.3 million, rising to RM99.9 million from RM61.7 million in the previous quarter, driven by economies of scale and product innovation. In addition, PAT recorded an increase of 66.4% or RM33.7 million, rising from RM50.8 million in the immediate preceding quarter to RM84.5 million. This sequential earnings acceleration was predominantly supported by the continued positive impact of the statutory income tax exemption received by the subsidiary, VTSB. \n\n B3 Prospect \n\n The Group anticipates a favourable business environment heading into the second half of 2026, supported by continued investments in AI and data centre infrastructure. According to Gartner's updated June 2026 forecast, worldwide semiconductor revenue is projected to reach a record US$1.56 trillion in 2026, representing year-on-year growth of 92.2%, driven primarily by strong demand for memory, AI accelerators and networking semiconductors. Memory revenue is forecast to exceed US$830 billion and account for more than half of total semiconductor revenue. \n\n Against this backdrop, the Group continues to prioritise its advanced packaging and high-precision inspection and testing solutions to address the increasing complexity of AI accelerators, HBM and advanced packaging technologies. The Group remains focused on developing next-generation, high-resolution machine vision solutions to meet the increasingly stringent quality and process-control requirements of semiconductor manufacturers, positioning itself to capture emerging opportunities arising from the industry's continued expansion. \n\n While remaining optimistic about the long-term prospects of its automated inspection business, the Group will continue to exercise prudent cost management and operational discipline to mitigate potential risks arising from foreign exchange volatility and geopolitical uncertainties. These initiatives are intended to strengthen the Group's operational resilience while enabling it to capitalise on favourable industry trends and evolving customer demand. \n\n B4 Profit forecast, profit guarantee and internal targets \n\n The Group did not provide any profit forecast, profit guarantee and internal targets in any public document or any announcements made. \n\n B5 Tax expense \n\n INDIVIDUAL QUARTER CUMULATIVE QUARTER \n\n Corresponding Corresponding Current preceding \n\n Current quarter preceding period-to-date period-to-date ended quarter ended ended ended \n\n 30-Jun-26 30-Jun-25 30-Jun-26 30-Jun-25 RM'000 RM'000 RM'000 RM'000 \n\n Current tax 15,451 10,100 26,327 13,607\n\n The effective tax rate of the Group for the current financial period is lower than the statutory tax rate of 24%. This was mainly due to tax incentives enjoyed by its wholly-owned subsidiary, VTSB. The current provision of income tax is in respect of certain non-business income and non-tax exempted income generated from non-pioneer products and services. \n\n VTSB has been granted an income tax exemption by the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (\"MIDA\") for a period of five years, extendable for a further five years, for activities related to the development and production of 4D Advanced Industrial Automation Systems, Machines, Equipment, and related modules integrated with self-healing capabilities for semiconductor advanced packaging and AI Smart Factories. \n\n B6 Status of corporate proposals announced \n\n There was no corporate proposal announced and not completed as at the date of this report. \n\n B7 Group borrowings \n\n As at \n\n 30-Jun-26 RM'000 \n\n As at \n\n 30-Jun-26 USD'000 \n\n As at \n\n 30-Jun-25 RM'000 \n\n As at \n\n 30-Jun-25 USD'000 \n\n Term loans - secured \n\n Short-term borrowings \n\n 21,505 \n\n 5,284 \n\n 22,417 \n\n 5,313 \n\n Long-term borrowings \n\n 60,733 \n\n 14,922 \n\n 84,878 \n\n 20,130 \n\n 82,238 \n\n 20,206 \n\n 107,295 \n\n 25,443 \n\n Exchange rate \n\n 4.07 \n\n 4.22 \n\n The higher term loan balance as at 30 June 2025 was attributable to the drawdown of an additional term loan to finance the construction of Campus 3.0 in Batu Kawan. \n\n The effective interest rates for the current period ended ranged from 4.73% to 4.77% as compared to 5.32% to 5.35% for the corresponding preceding period. \n\n B8 Material litigation \n\n As of the date of this announcement, the Group is not engaged in any material litigation and the Board of Directors does not have any knowledge of any proceedings pending or threatened against the Group. \n\n B9 Dividend \n\n The Company proposed a final dividend of 1.18 sen per share exempt from income tax for the year ended 31 December 2025 on 29 April 2026.
